description: First 50 seeds only - testing "starting well" quality

scoring_criteria.9: Perfect native speech in both languages
scoring_criteria.1-2: Marginal, no one would say this

phrases.english: You wanted to ask, right?
phrases.other: 何か聞きたかったですね
phrases.notes: Good. Japanese uses nanika (something) which slightly differs from the direct 'ask' sense but is natural. The ne ending for confirmation is appropriate.

phrases.english: It is easy to speak Japanese.
phrases.other: 日本語を簡単に話せます
phrases.notes: Functional but structure is slightly off. More natural: 日本語を話すのは簡単です or 日本語は簡単に話せます. Current version uses wo with kantan-ni adverbially which works but feels textbook.

phrases.english: Why don't you want to stop speaking Japanese?
phrases.other: なぜ日本語を話すのをやめたくありませんか
phrases.notes: Grammatically correct but awkward in both languages. Double negative construction is convoluted. English is unnatural - 'Why do you keep wanting to speak Japanese?' would be better. Japanese is technically correct but stilted.

phrases.english: speak a little Japanese now
phrases.other: 今少し日本語を話します
phrases.notes: Good fragment. Japanese word order is natural (ima sukoshi nihongo wo hanashimasu). Works well for practice.

phrases.english: I'm not sure if I can remember a word.
phrases.other: 言葉を覚えられるかどうかわかりません
phrases.notes: Excellent. Natural use of ka dou ka construction. Both languages sound authentic.

phrases.english: want to try very hard today
phrases.other: 今日とても頑張りたいです
phrases.notes: Excellent. Ganbaru is perfect for 'try hard'. Natural in both languages.

phrases.english: today don't know what will happen
phrases.other: 今日何が起こるかわからない
phrases.notes: Good. Japanese is natural with plain form wakaranai. English fragment is a bit choppy but acceptable.

phrases.english: She wants to learn quickly.
phrases.other: 彼女は早く覚えたいです
phrases.notes: Excellent. Oboetai (want to memorize/learn) is natural. Hayaku placement is good.

phrases.english: He wants to practice quickly.
phrases.other: 彼は早く練習したいです
phrases.notes: Excellent. Renshuu shitai is natural. Good parallel to phrase 8.

phrases.english: As if I'm ready to go.
phrases.other: 行ける準備ができているように
phrases.notes: Awkward in both languages. English 'as if' is incomplete. Japanese you ni at end suggests manner/comparison but sentence feels truncated. Would benefit from context.

phrases.english: I probably can't remember easily.
phrases.other: 簡単には覚えられないでしょう
phrases.notes: Excellent. Deshou for probability is natural. Kantan-ni wa with negative is idiomatic.

phrases.english: as much as possible
phrases.other: できるだけ
phrases.notes: Perfect. Dekiru dake is the exact idiomatic equivalent.

phrases.english: when he speaks Japanese
phrases.other: 彼が日本語を話す時に
phrases.notes: Excellent. Toki ni construction is correct and natural.

phrases.english: when she learns Japanese
phrases.other: 彼女が日本語を学ぶ時に
phrases.notes: Excellent. Parallel to phrase 13. Manabu is slightly formal but correct.

phrases.english: He wants to learn her name before he has to go.
phrases.other: 彼は行かなければならない前に彼女の名前を覚えたいです
phrases.notes: Awkward word order in Japanese. 'Mae ni' (before) should come after the time clause, not split the sentence. Better: 行かなければならない前に、彼は彼女の名前を覚えたいです. Also very long and complex for early seeds.

phrases.english: as soon as you can speak
phrases.other: できるだけ早く話す
phrases.notes: Mistranslation. 'Dekiru dake hayaku' means 'as quickly as possible', not 'as soon as you can'. For 'as soon as', Japanese would use 話せるようになったらすぐ or similar.

phrases.english: I don't know if I can speak Japanese.
phrases.other: 日本語が話せるかどうかわかりません
phrases.notes: Excellent. Ka dou ka construction is perfect. Ga particle with potential form is correct.

phrases.english: Meeting everyone takes too much time.
phrases.other: 皆に会うのに時間がかかりすぎます
phrases.notes: Excellent. No ni for purpose, jikan ga kakari-sugimasu for 'takes too much time' is idiomatic.

phrases.english: I want to become able to speak now.
phrases.other: 今話せるようになりたい
phrases.notes: Good. You ni naru is correct for 'become able to'. English is slightly awkward but grammatically valid.

phrases.english: He speaks Japanese more.
phrases.other: 彼はもっと日本語を話します
phrases.notes: Good. Motto placement is natural. English 'more' at end is slightly awkward but understandable.

phrases.english: I want to practice speaking.
phrases.other: 話す練習をしたいです
phrases.notes: Excellent. Hanasu renshuu wo shitai is natural and commonly used.

phrases.english: anything to speak
phrases.other: 何も話す
phrases.notes: Problematic. 'Nani mo' with positive verb is incorrect - nani mo requires negative verb. Should be 何か話す (something to speak) or needs restructuring. English fragment is also vague.

phrases.english: he doesn't want to be quiet
phrases.other: 彼は静かにしたくありません
phrases.notes: Good. Shizuka ni suru (to be/become quiet) with negative tai form is natural.

phrases.english: Did he want to learn anything?
phrases.other: 彼は何か覚えたかったですか
phrases.notes: Excellent. Nanika with positive verb is correct. Past tense tai form (takatta) is natural.

phrases.english: He likes speaking Japanese.
phrases.other: 彼は日本語を話すのが好きです
phrases.notes: Perfect. No ga suki desu is the standard construction for liking to do something.

phrases.english: Did she want to learn Japanese?
phrases.other: 彼女は日本語を覚えたかったですか
phrases.notes: Excellent. Parallel to phrase 24. Natural question form.

phrases.english: she is learning Japanese
phrases.other: 彼女は日本語を学んでいます
phrases.notes: Excellent. Te-iru form for ongoing action is correct. Manandeimasu is natural.

phrases.english: what the answer is
phrases.other: 答えが何か
phrases.notes: Good embedded question fragment. Kotae ga nani ka works as a clause. Could also be 答えは何か.

phrases.english: At the moment she is a little tired.
phrases.other: 今彼女は少し疲れています
phrases.notes: Excellent. Tsukareteimasu for current state of being tired is correct. Word order is natural.

phrases.english: other people speak Japanese
phrases.other: 他の人が日本語を話す
phrases.notes: Excellent. Hoka no hito ga is natural. Plain form hanasu works for subordinate clauses or statements.

phrases.english: as often as possible
phrases.other: できるだけ頻繁に
phrases.notes: Good. Hinpan ni (frequently) with dekiru dake is correct, though hinpan is somewhat formal/written. Dekiru dake yoku might be more conversational.

phrases.english: ask you something
phrases.other: あなたに何か聞き
phrases.notes: Incomplete. Kiki is the stem form - needs completion (kikitai, kikimasu, etc.). Fragment is unusable as-is.

phrases.english: speak a little Japanese
phrases.other: 少し日本語を話します
phrases.notes: Excellent. Natural word order. Good basic sentence.

phrases.english: as soon as you can learn
phrases.other: できるだけ早く覚える
phrases.notes: Same issue as phrase 16. 'Dekiru dake hayaku' means 'as quickly as possible', not 'as soon as you can'. Mistranslation.

phrases.english: as much as possible
phrases.other: できるだけ
phrases.notes: Perfect. Duplicate of phrase 12. Dekiru dake is exact idiomatic match.

phrases.english: want to know her name
phrases.other: 彼女の名前を知りたい
phrases.notes: Excellent. Shiritai is natural. Good basic phrase.

phrases.english: Will she help me speak Japanese?
phrases.other: 彼女は日本語を話すのを手伝ってくれますか
phrases.notes: Excellent. Te-kureru for receiving help is natural. No wo tetsudatte is correct structure.

phrases.english: Did he want to speak?
phrases.other: 彼は話したかったですか
phrases.notes: Excellent. Past tense tai form in question is natural.

phrases.english: want to learn her name quickly
phrases.other: 彼女の名前を早く覚えたい
phrases.notes: Excellent. Hayaku placement and oboetai are natural.

phrases.english: I don't know if I can practice all day.
phrases.other: 一日中練習できるかどうかわかりません
phrases.notes: Excellent. Ichinichi-juu (all day) is natural. Ka dou ka construction is correct.

phrases.english: she doesn't want anything
phrases.other: 彼女は何もしたくありません
phrases.notes: Functional but slight semantic mismatch. 'Nani mo shitakunai' means 'doesn't want to do anything', not 'doesn't want anything (as object)'. For wanting objects, would need 何も欲しくありません.

phrases.english: looking forward to meeting
phrases.other: 会うのを楽しみにしています
phrases.notes: Perfect. Tanoshimi ni shiteimasu is the exact idiomatic expression for looking forward to.

phrases.english: become able to speak
phrases.other: 話せるようになる
phrases.notes: Perfect. You ni naru with potential form is exactly right.

phrases.english: I do not want to speak Japanese.
phrases.other: 日本語を話したくないです
phrases.notes: Excellent. Negative tai form is natural. English is slightly formal but correct.

phrases.english: Today I wouldn't like to guess.
phrases.other: 今日当てたくありません
phrases.notes: Functional. 'Wouldn't like to' is awkward English (better: 'don't want to'). Japanese atetaku arimasen (don't want to guess) is correct but ateru for guessing is slightly unusual - context-dependent.

phrases.english: But we want to meet at six this evening.
phrases.other: でも私たちは今晩6時に会いたいです
phrases.notes: Excellent. Demo at start is natural. Konban rokuji ni aitai is correct.

phrases.english: I'm not trying to finish as quickly as possible.
phrases.other: できるだけ早く終わらせようとしているわけではありません
phrases.notes: Good but complex. Wake de wa arimasen for 'it's not that...' is sophisticated. Long but grammatically correct. Appropriate for advanced learners.

phrases.english: She is looking forward to it.
phrases.other: 彼女は楽しみにしています
phrases.notes: Perfect. Natural and idiomatic.

phrases.english: She has to go soon.
phrases.other: 彼女はもうすぐ行かなければなりません
phrases.notes: Excellent. Mou sugu (soon) + nakereba narimasen (must) is natural and correct.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to be quiet when other people are here.
phrases.other: 他の人がいる時に彼は静かにしたくありません
phrases.notes: Good. Complex sentence handled well. Word order is acceptable though slight reordering might be more natural.

phrases_below_5.english: as soon as you can speak
phrases_below_5.reason: Mistranslation: 'dekiru dake hayaku' means 'as quickly as possible', not 'as soon as you can'
Grammatical error: 'nani mo' requires negative verb. This is incorrect Japanese.
Incomplete: 'kiki' is stem form, needs verb ending (kikitai, kikimasu, etc.)

phrases_below_5.english: as soon as you can learn
phrases_below_5.other: できるだけ早く覚える
phrases_below_5.reason: Mistranslation: same issue as phrase 16 - 'dekiru dake hayaku' means 'as quickly as possible'

worst_3_phrases.reason: CRITICAL ERROR: 'nani mo' (nothing/anything) MUST be used with negative verbs in Japanese. 'Nani mo hanasu' is ungrammatical. Should be 何か話す (something to speak) or restructured entirely. Both English and Japanese are vague fragments that don't communicate clearly.

worst_3_phrases.english: as soon as you can speak
worst_3_phrases.reason: SEMANTIC MISMATCH: 'Dekiru dake hayaku' literally means 'as quickly/fast as possible' - it's about speed, not timing. 'As soon as you can speak' implies the moment when ability is gained, requiring constructions like 話せるようになったらすぐ (as soon as you become able to speak).

worst_3_phrases.english: as soon as you can learn
worst_3_phrases.other: できるだけ早く覚える
worst_3_phrases.reason: SAME MISTRANSLATION as phrase 16: conflates 'as quickly as possible' with 'as soon as'. This is a systematic error in the course content that should be addressed.

strengths: Strong use of ka dou ka (whether or not) construction
Correct application of tai-form for desires
Natural use of idiomatic expressions (dekiru dake, tanoshimi ni shiteimasu)
Good particle usage in most phrases
weaknesses: Systematic mistranslation of 'as soon as' vs 'as quickly as possible'
Critical nani mo + positive verb error (phrase 22)
Some overly complex sentences for early seeds (phrase 15)
recommendations: Fix 'dekiru dake hayaku' translations - this appears twice and is incorrect
Review early seed complexity - phrase 15 may be too advanced for seed 25
